articles.headline: NFL Week 7: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday's games
articles.description: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 7.
articles.body:
The Sunday slate for Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season kicked off in Paris between the Saints and Steelers. Pittsburgh dominated in the run game, with Jaylen Warren leading the way on 18 carries for 101 yards, and the Steelers held off New Orleans in the NFL's first game in France.

Keep checking back as the afternoon slate of games kicks off, and our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detail everything else you need to know for teams that played Sunday. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Michael Florio also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup.

Let's get to it with the biggest lessons from Sunday.

Jump to:

PIT-NO

Catch up on Thursday's game:

NE-CHI

Pittsburgh 16, New Orleans 10

Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Steelers

Are the Steelers embracing their RB-led identity on offense? This game was right on time for the Steelers, whose running game properly supported their 42-year-old quarterback with 5.4 yards per carry. Jaylen Warren is the Steelers' best offensive player. Opposing coaches agree. And, for the fourth game this season, he produced 125-plus scrimmage yards, tying Kansas City's Kenneth Walker III for most in the NFL. This offensive line is opening holes for Warren and Rico Dowdle, the bruising complement to Warren's burst. They closed out the game late, and Pittsburgh ran 12 plays for 79 yards with six offensive linemen on the field today (had zero such plays entering the game). The passing game needs more explosive plays. But the running game can handle the rest.

Trend to watch: The Steelers' second-half adjustments defensively were encouraging. The Steelers were blitz-heavy in the first half, coming for quarterback Tyler Shough 50% of the time. Shough went 9-of-10 for 98 yards and a TD on those plays. So, defensive coordinator Patrick Graham dropped the Steelers into coverage more often in the second half, blitzing twice on 21 attempts -- both blitzes coming on the Saints' failed final offensive drive. Timely defense for the Steelers, who held the Saints to 18 rushing yards, the fewest for New Orleans since 1999. -- Jeremy Fowler

Next game: vs. Browns (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Saints

Can the Saints get healthy and get help coming out of their Week 8 bye? New Orleans quarterback Tyler Shough entered Sunday's game with an injured non-throwing hand, and he appeared to take a hit on his throwing hand as well. Shough could likely use the week of rest to get healthy, but he's not the only one. The Saints don't have a run game and have relied heavily on Shough. Could running back Travis Etienne and wide receiver Jordyn Tyson make their debuts after the bye to give the Saints much-needed help? The Saints are also missing left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr., who went on injured reserve in late September following ankle surgery.

articles.headline: Aaron Rodgers breaks tie with Peyton Manning for third-most TD passes
articles.description: Aaron Rodgers threw one touchdown pass to move alone to third all-time on the NFL's career list in Pittsburgh's 16-10 win over the Saints on Sunday in the NFL's first regular-season game in France.
articles.body:
SAINT-DENIS, France -- Aaron Rodgers threw one touchdown pass to move to third on the NFL's career list and Chris Boswell kicked three field goals in Pittsburgh's 16-10 win over the New Orleans Saints on Sunday in the NFL's first regular-season game in France.

Jaylen Warren rushed for 101 yards and Rodgers completed 19 of 30 passes for 212 yards and scrambled for a key first down late in fourth quarter as the Steelers (5-2) won their third straight game.

Rodgers' 4-yard touchdown pass to 6-foot-7, 265-pound tight end Darnell Washington -- with 5-foot-11 cornerback Kool-Aid McKinstry in coverage -- put the Steelers up 10-3.

The scoring pass broke a tie with Peyton Manning on the all-time touchdown pass list. Rodgers now sits alone at third with 540 touchdown passes in his career.

Earlier on the drive, Rodgers moved in the pocket and found DK Metcalf for a 51-yard completion to the New Orleans 4. NFL France called it "quel caviar d'Aaron Rodgers."

The Saints then tied it at 10-10 on Tyler Shough's 1-yard touchdown pass to Devaughn Vele on fourth-and-goal.

Linebacker Payton Wilson had a red zone interception of Tyler Shough in the third quarter and the Saints (2-5) couldn't recover. New Orleans rushed for just 18 yards.

With the Saints threatening on their opening drive of the second half, Wilson stepped in front of a short pass intended for Chris Olave. The Steelers got in field goal position and Boswell was good from 39 yards for a 16-10 lead.

Patrick Queen sacked Shough on third down to stall a New Orleans drive with under seven minutes left in the fourth quarter.

Shough completed 30 of 38 passes for 278 yards, one touchdown and the interception.

Just before halftime, Rodgers was sacked by Carl Granderson on third down, and with 15 seconds left and no timeouts, the Steelers offense ran to the sideline. Boswell sprinted on and kicked a 47-yard field goal to give Pittsburgh a 13-10 lead at the half.

Attendance was 78,488 at Stade de France.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Iraola era at Liverpool finally has lift off thanks to big-money forwards
articles.description: Two years ago, the Arne Slot project took off with a win over Brighton. Has the same thing just happened for Andoni Iraola?
articles.body:
LIVERPOOL, England -- It was an autumn afternoon on Nov. 2 2024 against Brighton & Hove Albion that Liverpool started to believe. A stirring victory over Fabian Hürzeler's side provided the launchpad for a new managerial era under Arne Slot at Anfield.

Almost two years on, Liverpool's 2-0 win against that same opponent might also be remembered as the day that Andoni Iraola's Reds' tenure began in earnest. Many of the personnel have changed -- including, of course, the man in the Anfield dugout -- but Sunday's triumph felt like a potentially defining moment for a team quietly beginning to find their feet under their new head coach.

It was not the perfect Liverpool display, by any means. Brighton ended the afternoon with 1.35 expected goals (xG) compared to the Reds' 0.87, having enjoyed 64.4% of the possession.

And yet, it never really felt like Liverpool were at risk of surrendering the three points after an own goal from Pascal Gross and a deft finish from Alexander Isak gave the hosts a deserved first-half lead.

While both teams huffed and puffed, the second half was relegated to a relative non-event, opening the door for Liverpool to claim their first home Premier League win under Iraola and their first home victory in the competition since beating Crystal Palace 3-1 back in April.

"I'm very happy," Iraola said in his post-match news conference. "I'm happy with this fourth win [in a row]. I think today we had a very good opposition in front of us, similar to Villarreal the other day -- teams that are technically really good. I think today the key was how we started. We needed a strong start, to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels and be dangerous in transitions. I think we did that and it's been a different game to those where we conceded first."

Having developed a reputation for being perpetually slow starters in the Premier League, Liverpool took a different approach against Brighton, playing with the verve and intensity that has too often been lacking in recent times. Their front-footed approach did leave them susceptible to an early scare from Yasin Ayari, who should have done better when he blazed over the crossbar from a fine cutback from Gross.

But Gross' afternoon quickly went from bad to worse when, just a few minutes later, he diverted Florian Wirtz's strike into the back of his own net to put Liverpool in front. While Wirtz was not credited with the goal, his steady improvement has been one of the most encouraging aspects for Iraola in recent weeks and he impressed again against Brighton before being substituted in the second half.

It fell to Liverpool's two other big-money signing to double the hosts' lead in the 21st minute; the fleet-footed Bradley Barcola fizzing the ball into the path of Isak who tucked it away past Bart Verbruggen. Barcola now has five goal contributions in his last four games for Liverpool across all competitions, with his last two assists being converted by Isak.

articles.headline: 2027 NFL draft questions, latest intel, risers, CFB standouts
articles.description: What are the odds Trey'Dez Green -- who scored in his return -- ends up as TE1? What's a good comp for Dylan Stewart? Here's draft spin off CFB Week 8.
articles.body:
Week 8 of the 2026 college football season brought us a few more upsets, including BYU falling to UCF, Cincinnati topping Texas Tech, South Carolina shocking Tennessee and Wisconsin knocking off USC. We also had Indiana edging Michigan in overtime to avoid letdown, Texas hanging on against Ole Miss and Utah coming back to beat Houston.

What about the top 2027 NFL draft prospects? Who stood out? Yes, the draft is still about six months away, but our analysts are always looking down the road, taking early notes on top players and starting to stack their rankings for an exciting class.

With that in mind, Mel Kiper Jr. and Jordan Reid will size up college football action through a draft-centric lens on Sundays all season long. They are answering lingering questions on the best 2027 prospects, sharing insights from scouts, picking out risers to watch and pulling back the curtain on their evaluation process. Here is what they saw and heard through Week 8.

Jump to:

Week 8 | Week 7 | Week 6 | Week 5

Week 4 | Week 3 | Week 2

Oct. 25

Trey'Dez Green is back. What are the chances he'll be the TE1 of the class?

Reid: I'll give it a 40% chance. Green returned after missing the previous three games with a leg injury, finishing with five catches for 50 yards and a touchdown against Auburn. He has soft hands and can attack the middle of the defense with his 6-foot-7, 237-pound frame. His run-after-catch ability is one of his best assets, too. Green's consistency as a blocker remains a work in progress, but coach Lane Kiffin has expanded his role in that area, and there's no denying that the LSU passing game builds off his alignment versatility when he mixes it up as a run blocker.

I still have Green behind Oregon's Jamari Johnson in my tight end rankings, but if he's able to remain healthy and productive during the backstretch of the season, there's a realistic chance that he could be the first tight off the board because of his diverse skill set.

What is your best comp for Dylan Stewart at the next level?

Reid: Brian Burns coming out of Florida State. He officially measured at 6-foot-5 and 249 pounds, and Stewart is listed at 6-foot-5 and 250 pounds. And their games match. The No. 3 overall player on my latest board, Stewart has exceptional bend and closing speed to constantly pressure passers, and he also understands how to utilize his length as a run defender. An argument could be made that Stewart has the highest ceiling of any defensive prospect in this class.

In his second game off suspension, Stewart made one of the biggest plays of the game, forcing a fumble to help set up the Gamecocks' upset victory over Tennessee. It was his third forced fumble in two weeks and his second straight game with a sack. articles.body:
Bayern Munich forward Lennart Karl is being tracked by Arsenal, Manchester United and Liverpool, while United defender Leny Yoro is on the radar of AC Milan. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United defender Leny Yoro is on the radar of AC Milan ahead of the summer, says Calciomercato. Yoro, 20, has struggled since moving from Lille for €62 million in 2024, but former United boss Ruben Amorim is keen to bring him to San Siro to add depth to his defense. A fee of around €50 million is expected to be enough for the France international to move on.

- Arsenal, Manchester United and Liverpool are monitoring Bayern Munich forward Lennart Karl, following concerns over his game time, according to TEAMtalk. Despite signing a new long-term deal earlier this year, the 18-year-old Germany international has made nine appearances this season -- scoring once and adding an assist -- and could consider an exit if his role does not expand.

- Trent Alexander-Arnold is not currently considered a concrete target for Liverpool as they evaluate future right-back options, reports Football Insider. Although the 28-year-old has experienced limited minutes at Real Madrid due to competition from Denzel Dumfries and Federico Valverde, there is no active movement toward an Anfield return.

- Tottenham Hotspur and Newcastle United have made inquiries regarding AC Milan duo Fikayo Tomori and Ruben Loftus-Cheek ahead of January, TEAMtalk reports. The Rossoneri are open to letting both players leave, with 28-year-old defender Tomori featuring just three times under Ruben Amorim and 30-year-old midfielder Loftus-Cheek making eight appearances across all competitions.

- Tottenham Hotspur will demand a hefty transfer fee for the transfer of right back Pedro Porro amid reported interest from Real Madrid and Barcelona, according to Diario AS. The spotlight was on struggling Manchester United as they welcomed AFC Bournemouth to Old Trafford without star player Bruno Fernandes in the XI, after he was dropped for his post-match comments last week, but it didn't help as United lost 3-0 to pile the pressure on manager Michael Carrick.

Elsewhere, Liverpool beat high-flying Brighton & Hove Albion 2-0 at Anfield, while Crystal Palace lost 2-0 to Newcastle United and Hull City drew 1-1 with Brentford.

articles.headline: Sunday's fantasy basketball adds and bets to make in the NBA
articles.description: Jim McCormick breaks down Sunday's slate, highlighting the fantasy streamers to add and bets to make.
articles.body:
ESPN's basketball daily cheat sheet is your pregame destination before you lock in daily fantasy and betting decisions for that night's games. Here you'll find our top insights for the slate, including players to target for your daily fantasy rosters, along with game-by-game injury reports.

What you need to know for Sunday

A seven-game Sunday slate features a series of potential competitive contests. Only one game on the docket claims a double-digit point spread -- a departure from a Saturday field that was full of large lines. The marquee matchup of the day features the Minnesota Timberwolves hosting the Toronto Raptors in a meeting of deep, darkhorse contenders.

Close games bode well for developing fantasy and betting angles, as rotations and workloads prove more predictable in competitive games. A good place to start during a busy day of basketball is the injury report, which tells us that we won't see Paolo Banchero, Zach Edey or Jalen Duren playing for their respective teams. Joel Embiid, meanwhile, is set to rest for the second leg of a back-to-back series for the Philadelphia 76ers.

While we're still learning how each rotation and coaching staff will react to the absence of big names from the gameplan, we can proactively make some decisions based on precedent and prediction. 

For the Orlando Magic, a proven veteran big man is due for more minutes and work in the wake of Banchero's ankle injury, as you'll read below. What will Memphis do sans Edey? How will Detroit cope with being sans their interior anchor in South Philly tonight? 

And, those 76ers don't have a one-to-one backup for Embiid like they did in seasons past in the form of Andre Drummond. They will instead likely turn to a collective and small-ball looks -- possible even some featuring LeBron at center. We'll learn a lot today about all of these sides, which can serve us in future slates, as well.

With an eye toward uncovering compelling betting angles and fantasy decisions, let's take a look at the day ahead in the NBA.

Fantasy stream team -- widely available players worth adding

 Wendell Carter Jr., C, Orlando Magic (rostered in 23.5% of ESPN leagues)

With Banchero in street clothes for tonight's tilt with the New York Knicks, Carter should see more minutes, rebounding chances, and post touches as a result. The Knicks lack the interior defense and rebounding from last season's run, supporting confidence in double-double upside for this veteran big.

Paul Reed, C/PF, Detroit Pistons (14.2%)

Assuming Philadelphia decides to rest Embiid in the second game of a back-to-back, they will likely turn to a number of different looks to cover for him. Reed, who will consume a good bit of the work reserved for Duren, would then be facing a 76ers lineup badly lack rebounding acumen, establishing a nice floor for this active and unique frontcourt talent. It also helps that there is a fun narrative in play, as "B-ball Paul" began his career in Philly.

articles.headline: Michael Carrick woe worsens, Man United lose to Bournemouth
articles.description: The pressure on Michael Carrick grew as Manchester United slumped to a limp 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth on Sunday.
articles.body:
The pressure on Michael Carrick grew as Manchester United slumped to a limp 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth on Sunday.

Carrick had left Bruno Fernandes out of the team for the Premier League clash -- and didn't bring him off the bench -- after his criticism of the team's tactics following a 4-1 humbling against Como in midweek in the Champions League.

But with Fernandes looking on from the bench, his teammates were soundly beaten at Old Trafford.

Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson scored the goals for the away side to leave Carrick's job under more scrutiny than ever.

Carrick later told Sky Sports about leaving Fernandes on the bench: "There are always times in games when you try to make decisions to try and change the course of play, to try to make a difference. These were the decisions that we made today."

He added: "It's a tough situation. I won't hide from it. What's next? I really don't know. I'll do what's best for this football club, I've said that all along and I don't change that now. I love what I do and I love the position I am in. I feel the responsibility."

articles.headline: Liverpool's front four get firing as Andoni Iraola's men outplay Brighton
articles.description: Liverpool's expensively-assembled front four finally clicked into gear as they beat Brighton 2-0 to record their first home Premier League win of the season.
articles.body:
Liverpool's expensively-assembled front four finally clicked into gear as they beat Brighton 2-0 to record their first home Premier League win of the season.

The trio of £100 million-plus signings Alexander Isak, Bradley Barcola, Florian Wirtz -- and Cody Gakpo -- found a connection which fans have been hoping will succeed in breaking down defences against whom they struggled during their disappointing title defence.

They do not come more miserly than the Seagulls as Fabian Hurzeler's side may be the top flight's leading scorers but they also know how to keep the back door tightly shut and these were the first goals conceded in all competitions in over nine hours.

Wirtz was denied the credit for the 17th-minute opener due to the deflection off Pascal Groß but there was no doubting Isak's sixth goal in seven league appearances four minutes later from a Barcola cross.

Strong contributions from the France international and Gakpo on the flanks ensured Brighton were never entirely comfortable in a first half in which they started the brighter.

By the 77th minute only Gakpo remained but with the visitors starting to cause problems -- and Chelsea arriving on Wednesday in the Carabao Cup -- changes were necessary.

The other performance of note came from on-loan Barcelona defender Ronald Araujo.

A centre-back playing on the right, he crossed for the first goal and continued to enhance his cult status with a header while flat out on the floor to deny Maxim De Cuyper a goalscoring opportunity just after going 2-0 up and a no-nonsense clearance which was close to putting Malick Yalcouyé into the first row of the Main Stand.

Brighton may have fared better had Yasin Ayari not blazed over the first chance of the game after Diego Gomez's pass released Groß but once Liverpool were ahead confidence flowed through them.

This was a fourth win in a row in all competitions, and a third in four in the league lifted them into fourth, six points behind Manchester City and Arsenal.

Brighton may have had two days' less rest after their Europa League exploits but only three of that team were retained and even the loss of right-back Ferdi Kadioglu to injury after just six minutes did not dampen their verve.

But once Ayari wasted his opportunity in front of the Kop, Liverpool heeded the warning and when the excellent Araujo's cross rebounded off Groß, Wirtz's quick reactions saw the ball divert off the Seagulls midfielder to beat beat Bart Verbruggen.

In the next four minutes Gakpo had a shot saved and Isak fired over before scoring the second.

Barcola charged down Olivier Boscagli's clearance and crossed for the Sweden striker to produce a poacher's finish, scoring in three consecutive games for the first time since January 2025.

Ayari's low, curled shot hit the post with goalkeeper Alisson Becker having decided it was going wide but Araujo had the last say of the first half by forcing a save out of Verbruggen.

              BOTTOM LINE: Miami aims to end its three-game losing streak when the Heat play Dallas.
